CIVL 1000.description: A compulsory, one year course for students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. This is the first course of the APD course series (CIVL1000/2000/3000/4000) for Year 1 students. CIVL 1100.title: Discovering Civil and Environmental Engineering
CIVL 1100.description: A general overview of civil and environmental engineering, infrastructure development and engineering ethics is provided. The course includes both lectures and laboratory sessions, where the laboratory sessions are primarily directed to students who require the development of feasible conceptual solutions for the analysis and design of the basic problems in structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering.
cilos: Demonstrate a broad overview of civil and environmental engineering, including details of their major disciplines, importance and challenges through lectures
Demonstrate an overview of history and future of infrastructure developments

Demonstrate an understanding of the role of civil and environmental engineers in our society and the fundamental principle of engineering ethics and civil engineers’ obligations towards the public, employers and the profession
Demonstrate knowledge of basic physical concepts in structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering
Identify and analyze of the basic problems associated with the design of structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering
Develop feasible conceptual solutions for the analysis of the basic problems in structural, geotechnical and environmental engineering
Acquire and apply skills in written presentation of scientific and technical information

CIVL 1121.title: Introduction to Computation for Civil Engineers
CIVL 1121.description: This course aims to introduce Civil Engineering students with a basic understanding of the computation role in solving real-world Civil Engineering problems, and provide a broad overview of the computation for their engineering career. It will give students fundamental capabilities to write small programs that allow them to accomplish useful goals. The class will use the Python programming language.

Computational Efficiency: Students will understand basic concepts of computational efficiency and be able to optimize simple programs.
Software Tool Utilization: Gain experience using relevant software tools and libraries commonly used in civil engineering computations.
Data Manipulation and Analysis: Use Python to manipulate, analyze, and visualize engineering-related data.

CIVL 1140.title: Environment and Society: Sustainable Development Goals and Carbon Neutrality
CIVL 1140.description: Introduction of up-to-date environmental issues in both local and global scales and elaboration of essential concepts in physical, chemical, biological and societal aspects will be provided for students to understand the issues related to sustainable development goals and carbon neutrality. Students will learn to apply and evaluate approaches in science, engineering, management, and social science for enhancing the quality of our water, air, land, eco-systems, and urban development. The objective of this course is to equip our next-generation leaders in different disciplines with environmental awareness and knowledge of practical solutions to environmental issues. Upon completing this course, students should be able to make responsible decisions and actions, with due consideration of environmental sustainability and long-term decarbonization. By reviewing and discussing essential concepts and practical applications, students will conduct group projects and deliver presentations of their self-directed focus studies of emerging environmental issues in our society.
cilos: Explain and apply the basic principles of science and methods of scientific inquiry in environmental quality control and improvement
Evaluate the social and philosophical implications of scientific discoveries and technological development in environmental quality control and improvement
Apply professional knowledge in solving engineering problems related to environmental quality control and improvement
Communicate and present key environmental issues and their solutions effectively
Apply ethics in environmental quality control and improvement as responsible citizens and decision makers

CIVL 1160.title: Civil Engineering and Modern Society
CIVL 1160.description: An introduction to civil engineering practice and infrastructure development, with an emphasis on Hong Kong projects. The basic principles, materials and technology used in typical civil engineering works such as foundations, buildings, bridges, slopes and water supply systems, etc. Infrastructure management and maintenance issues; social-economic aspects of large-scale civil engineering projects such as environmental protection, urban planning and development, etc.

CIVL 1161.title: Building the Future: Civil Engineering Challenges & Solutions
CIVL 1161.description: This course offers an exploration of civil engineering practices in Hong Kong, with a focus on the solutions engineers implement to address current infrastructure challenges. Students will develop an understanding of how advanced technology and sustainable practices are influencing the built environment. The course includes a collaborative group project that encourages students to critically analyze recent civil engineering developments globally. Additionally, students may participate in optional site visits to ongoing civil engineering projects and operational facilities, providing practical insights into the skills and competencies necessary for designing, constructing, and managing engineering projects. By engaging in this course, students will gain knowledge and skills relevant to addressing the infrastructure needs of the future while considering sustainability and resilience in engineering practices.
cilos: Articulate the vital role of civil engineers in designing, constructing, and maintaining essential infrastructure that supports both urban and rural development; and recognize how these contributions are integral to societal progress and quality of life

Acquire a comprehensive understanding of the engineering processes involved in the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure; and develop the ability to critically analyze each phase and appreciate the complexities and interdependencies inherent in civil engineering projects

Demonstrate an informed appreciation of the history of civil engineering development in Hong Kong, including key milestones and innovations; and analyze future technology development trends and plans in the field, considering the implications for sustainable development and urban resilience

Develop and apply data collection and analysis skills to identify, define, and solve engineering problems effectively; and utilize quantitative and qualitative methods to support decision-making processes in real-world scenarios

Analyze contemporary social issues related to infrastructure development from both engineering and humanistic perspectives; and engage in discussions with professional engineers to explore the ethical impacts of infrastructure projects, including the social unrest in Hong Kong, and reflect on the engineer's role in addressing these challenges

Cultivate teamwork and communication skills by participating in collaborative projects and discussions; and understand the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in addressing complex engineering challenges and promoting innovative solutions for the future

CIVL 1180.title: Monitoring Changing Climate from Space
CIVL 1180.description: This course introduces the fundamental principles of satellite remote sensing and its role in monitoring our changing climate and environment. It covers the science underlying remote sensing, various remote sensing methods and technologies, observational evidence of climate change from space, and use of satellite data to advance science understanding and assist decision-making. The characteristics of satellite data and common methods to process and analyze satellite data will be introduced.
cilos: Explain remote sensing principles, approaches, and methods
Describe satellite observations of climate change and associate the changes to human activities
Discuss and evaluate the complexity of physical science, and its limitation and future developments
Process, analyze, and interpret spatiotemporally varying data
Assess the soundness of climate-related policies using scientific knowledge policymaking
Write quantitative evidence-based reports with critical thinking and technical writing skills

CIVL 1190.title: Climate Change, Big History and Sustainability
CIVL 1190.description: Big History as an emerging interdisciplinary framework, provides a long-term perspective to see the world through reconstructing the history from the big bang all the way to the present. In such a longer time scale, overview of stars, planetary and species evolution, as well as concepts in climate change and how it is related to sustainability of the planet’s environment for its current inhabitants, including humanity, will be discussed. The physical science basis, impacts, risk, mitigation and adaptation measures of climate change will also be investigated (including technical and social solutions). For local and regional vulnerabilities, such as extreme weather events, sea levels rise, storm surge and coastal flooding, will be covered. The significance of collective learning under the big history framework, both as a driver for our exponentially growing impacts, as well as for better solutions, will be highlighted.
cilos: Analyze the historical contingencies of environmental impacts and atmospheric composition changes under the Big History perspective, focusing on the role of collective learning in industrial and economic development over the past 250 years
Apply physical principles to explain the science of star formation, planetary evolution, the greenhouse effect, and global climate change
Justify the rationales for climate change mitigation and adaptation measures adopted by governments and corporations, considering uncertainties in climate modeling
Synthesize observational evidence and modeling frameworks to interpret and argue for or against the occurrence of anthropogenic climate change

Apply Big History concepts, e.g., complexity and fragility and collective learning, to critically assess social, political, and economic implications of climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

Evaluate sustainability-related issues within the Big History framework, recognizing Homo sapiens’ role in ecosystem sustainability, and argue effectively on controversial climate-related topics for diverse audiences

CIVL 1210.title: Fundamental of Green Buildings
CIVL 1210.description: This course will dive into the fundamental elements of green building at two scales: the building scale and the city. Strategies and techniques that optimize various perspectives of green buildings will be taught and discussed. Students will learn how to achieve energy efficiency and sustainability in building design and operation, as well as the fundamental principles behind these designs.
cilos: Describe the concept of green buildings and measures to evaluate them
Explain energy efficient building design from both indoor and outdoor perspectives
Analyze the impact of buildings on environment with governing equations

CIVL 1210.title: Fundamental of Green Buildings
CIVL 1210.description: This course contains two parts. The first part is about indoor environment of green building. It covers the four aspects of indoor environment quality (thermal, indoor air quality, lighting, and acoustic), building energy load calculation and energy efficient design. The second part covers the interaction between building and outdoor environment. Principles of radiation exchange, heat transfer and surface energy balance in the context of urban environment are included.
cilos: Understand four major aspects of indoor environment quality and how to evaluate the indoor environment quality.
Understand energy efficient building design from both indoor and outdoor perspectives.
Analyze the impact of buildings on outdoor environment with the governing equations.
Describe the fundamental process and principle of indoor-outdoor thermal exchange.

CIVL 1220.title: Big Data for Smarter Cities
CIVL 1220.description: Students will discover the exciting world of smart cities. Smart cities and big data have become an integral part of our daily lives. With the advent of big data and artificial intelligence, we now have effective tools to understand and improve the quality of our urban environments. This course will provide a glimpse into the exciting advances in this field. Students will be introduced about the unique qualities of urban big data and the concepts on how to analyze it using powerful techniques like data visualization, data mining, and AI. With hands-on projects, students will see and appreciate how data science can help tackle real-world urban problems and make our cities more sustainable and livable.
cilos: Explain and discuss the concepts of the Smart City and Urban Data Science
Identify urban issues and analyze existing urban decisions
Evaluate basic data management, visualization, and analysis methods
Apply basic programming commands in urban data analytics
Apply data-driven thinking on urban studies or applications

CIVL 2020.description: A practical training course in an industrial simulated environment. For students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. Graded P, PP or F.

CIVL 2021.title: Industrial Training: BIM, Drawing, Surveying, and Sustainability
CIVL 2021.description: The course provides an introduction to building information modeling (BIM), engineering drawings, engineering surveying, and sustainability. It includes theoretical and practical training on BIM model creation and analyses, engineering drawing generation, and related topics such as BIM standards and digital smart construction. The course also includes an introduction to the theory and practice of engineering surveying, including the measurement of level differences, angles and distances using construction levels and total stations, with applications in building structures. In addition, the course offers safety training and environmental training as well. For CIVL and CIEV students only.
cilos: Understand the basics of BIM and CAD, and use BIM and CAD software for both buildings and civil infrastructure applications.
Draw BIM models and perform basic analyses using 3D BIM models.
Use a construction level to measure differences in heights, apply such techniques in settlement monitoring and land profile determination, and process the data collected to obtain reduced levels.

Use a total station to measure vertical and horizontal angles and slope distances, convert the collected data to 3D coordinates, and apply such techniques to the measurements of buildings and structures such as the HKUST Sundial.
Identify potential hazards and apply appropriate control measures with a positive safety attitude in civil and construction activities.
Understand the role of construction innovations and sustainable practices in improving productivity, safety, and environmental performance in the construction industry.
Identify common parameters for water and air quality assessment and demonstrate correct use of portable instruments for field measurement and sampling.

CIVL 2035.title: Mathematical Methods for Civil Engineers
CIVL 2035.description: This course provides a concise introduction to multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and differential equations with an emphasis on civil engineering applications. Main topics include vector operations, partial derivatives and gradients, maximum/minimum problems, line integrals, vector fields and potential functions; systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors; first and second order ODEs, Fourier series, Delta functions, Green’s functions (Duhamel integrals), and introduction to PDEs. Efficient computational and visualization tools such as graphing calculators and spreadsheets will also be introduced. For CIVL and CIEV students only.
cilos: Perform vector operations such as dot products and cross products, both by hand and using a graphing calculator, and explain the geometrical/physical meaning behind the computations.

Visualize functions of two variables, compute partial derivatives both by hand and using a graphing calculator, understand the meaning of directional derivatives, and solve problems involving maxima and minima.

Evaluate double and triple integrals, perform integration to obtain centroids, calculate area moments of inertia (/) through integration (for simple shapes) and using AutoCAD’s MASSPROP function (for complicated shapes), and appreciate the physical significance of / in bending of beams.
Formulate linear equations in terms of matrices and obtain solutions via matrix algebra, both by hand and using Excel’s matrix functions such as MMULT and MINVERSE.
Understand the eigenvalue problem, obtain eigenvalues and eigenvectors by hand, and by using numerical software when matrix size is large.

Perform line integrals and understand the concept of vector fields; construct potential functions in the context of elastic energy, generate stiffness matrices using repeated partial derivatives on the elastic energy, and utilize computer algebra systems to expedite such matrix assembly.

Solve first and second ODEs using various methods such as characteristic equations, Delta functions, Fourier series, Green’s functions (Duhamel integrals) and computer software such as deSolve; understand the relation between ODEs and Newton’s second law of motion.

Understand basic terminology of PDEs and recognize basic types of PDEs such as the wave equation, apply series method to solve selected PDEs arising in vibration theory, and visualize time behavior of solutions using a graphing calculator.

Apply physical models to perform stress calculations and determine deflection, including thermal effects, in structural members such as axially loaded bars, torsional rods and beams.
Analyze and design simple structural members and determinate systems such as trusses, torsional members and beams on foundations.

Identify and model non-deterministic problems in civil engineering, and the treatment thereof as related to engineering design and decision making.
Formulate probability models based on the developed stochastic concepts, and their relevance to design and decision problems in various areas of civil engineering.
Solve engineering problems involving inherent uncertainties via probabilistic modelling and statistical tools.
Acquire basic simulation skills to solve realistic engineering problems effectively.

CIVL 2170.description: This course will cover basic principles and techniques for analyzing engineering systems. It will entail an introduction to linear programs, network analysis, critical path method, benefit-cost and present value analyses of engineering projects.

Understand the effect of environmental and mechanical actions on the long-term behavior of materials.
Specify the appropriate construction material for a given project.
Make sound engineering judgements when new construction materials or modifications to existing construction materials are proposed.

cilos: Explore Career Opportunities in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Gain Awareness of Latest Professional Practices and Real-World Applications.
Prepare for Professional Growth in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Develop skills for effective job application and interview.

CIVL 3020.title: Internship Training
CIVL 3020.description: For students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. Internship training provides students the opportunity to gain professional experience and to apply theories to real-life situations. Students are required to complete a minimum of six weeks on-the-job training in civil engineering consulting firms, contractors, developers or relevant government departments, or an equivalent of 5-week mock construction training under the supervision of professional practitioners. Graded P or F.
cilos: Gain practical professional experience in civil engineering.
Apply the knowledge acquired from the academic studies to real- life engineering practice.
Develop an appreciation of the breadth of civil engineering.

CIVL 3210.title: Introduction to Construction Management
CIVL 3210.description: This course covers the basic knowledge, skills and techniques in construction management. It entails an introduction to the construction industry, initial and feasibility studies, impact assessment, tendering process, local statutory ordinances, contract strategy and management, cost estimation and control, project finance, resource allocation, and site safety. For CIVL and CIEV students only.
cilos: Understand the construction industry and different stages in a construction project.
Perform construction contract administration.
Conduct cost estimation, cost control and project financing.
Specify the responsibility of different parties in construction safety and project management.
Appreciate the breadth of engineering problems.
Formulate and solve construction engineering and management problems.

CIVL 3310.title: Structural Analysis
CIVL 3310.description: Structural forms and modeling, statically determinate structures, statically indeterminate structures, force and displacement methods, deflections of structures, influence lines, approximate analysis, energy methods.
cilos: Analyze the behavior of structural systems under loads or other external effect.
Evaluate and present the results of a structural analysis to support the design of structural components and systems.
Conduct laboratory tests, validate test results using various methods, and assess the discrepancies between test and analysis results.

CIVL 3320.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
CIVL 3320.description: Ultimate limit state design of reinforced concrete beams, slabs, columns, and beam-column joints; serviceability limit states of deflection and cracking.
cilos: Adopt the critical Ultimate Limit States and the Serviceability Limit States concerning deflection and cracking control and satisfy the pertinent design requirements.
Design reinforced concrete beams for flexure, shear, torsion and serviceability and provide proper detailing.
Design reinforced concrete slabs for flexure, shear, (punching) shear and serviceability.
Design reinforced concrete columns for Uniaxial and Biaxial Bending combined with Axial loading.

CIVL 3420.title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
CIVL 3420.description: Introduction to basic concepts of water quality, fundamentals of water and wastewater treatment processes, analysis of treatment process flowsheets, analysis of water quality management alternatives.
cilos: Understand the entireprocess from water supply to wastewater treatment and the respective regulations.
Describe thecharacteristics of supplied water and the municipal sewage and the typical unit processes used incorrespondingtreatments.
Understand the principal of the physicochemical and biological treatments.
Explain what the key parameters areto design the water and wastewater treatment units.
Develop basic lab skills for environmental engineering andlearn how to analyze and interpret results.

CIVL 3510.title: Hydrosystems Engineering
CIVL 3510.description: This course introduces basic and fundamental knowledge essential to the design and analysis of hydrosystems engineering problems (e,g., water supply, flood control, stormwater drainage, etc.). The course consists of two interrelated parts: hydrology and hydraulics. Hydrology covers various processes of water cycle (including precipitation, infiltration, rainfall-runoff modeling, and flow routings) that produce loads on hydrosystems. Hydraulics, on the other hand, applies fluid mechanics principles to the design and analysis the capacity of hydrosystems infrastructures such as pipe networks and channel networks as well as hydraulic machinery.
cilos: Apply mathematical and statistical methods to analyze random hydrometric data and time-varying nature flow processes.
Understand physical principles of fluid motions to analyze and model flow processes in hydrologic cycle.

Demonstrate appreciation about the interdisciplinary nature of hydrosystems engineering which also straddles across environmental engineering with regard to pollutant transport and geotechnical engineering on slope stability.
Use modern computing software to analyze flow in complex hydrosystems.
Be given hydrosystems engineering design and management problems to build up their ability for problem formulation and solution.

Appreciate the importance of water in sustainable development of human society and preservation of environment, including the contributions and possible disservice in natural hazard mitigation, through in-class discussions.

Demonstrate an understanding of contemporary issues and challenges of hydrosystems engineering design and management, such as tradeoff of cost, reliability, and sustainability of water development in different parts of the worlds.

CIVL 3610.title: Traffic and Transportation Engineering
CIVL 3610.description: For students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. Introduction to transportation systems; characteristics of transportation models; traffic flow fundamentals; geometric design of highways; travel demand analysis including trip generation, modal split and trip assignment.
cilos: Understand the fundamental theory and methods involved in traffic and transportation engineering, including traffic flow fundamentals, geometric design of highways, and transportation systems planning.
Make use of mathematical or quantitative methods to model components of the traffic and transportation system.

Apply the principles learned in this course for the analysis, design and operations of components of the transportation system, including traffic impact analysis, highway design, and transportation demand forecasting.

CIVL 3730.title: Fundamentals of Geotechnics
CIVL 3730.description: This course will focus on the geotechnical mechanics and associated soil behavior, including basic engineering geology, characteristics of soils, soil compaction, the principle of effective stress, shear strength of soils, the concept of critical state modeling, permeability, seepage problems, ground settlement and consolidation. The laboratory section consists of five different experiments. For CIVL and CIEV students under the four-year degree only.
cilos: Understand, formulate, and solve problems related to geotechnical engineering.
Conduct experiments, analyze and interpret results for geotechnical engineering design.
Apply modern engineering tools effectively and efficiently for geotechnical engineering analysis.
Develop technical competency for geotechnical engineering related design.

CIVL 3740.title: Geotechnical Analysis and Design
CIVL 3740.description: Introduction to geotechnical analysis and design including slope stability analysis, bearing capacity of soils, lateral earth pressures, design of retaining wall, shallow and piled foundations, geotechnical centrifuge modeling and field monitoring.
cilos: Understand the basic principles of soil mechanics.

Comprehend and apply the basic soil mechanics theories in the design of earth retaining structures, braced cuts or multi-propped excavations, shallow and deep foundations, slope stability and reinforced earth structures.
Improve the ability of solving geotechnical problems independently and scientifically.

CIVL 4000.title: Academic and Professional Development for Civil and Environmental Engineering IV
CIVL 4000.description: Continuation of CIVL 3000. A compulsory, one year course for students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. This course is designed to provide academic advising to students and/or to develop students' interpersonal skills in handling technical and non-technical issues in their professional careers. Graded P, PP or F.
cilos: Explore Career Opportunities in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Gain Awareness of Latest Professional Practices and Real-World Applications.
Prepare for Professional Growth in Civil and Environmental Engineering.
Develop skills for effective job application and interview.

CIVL 4100.title: Special Topics
CIVL 4100.description: Selected topics in Civil Engineering of current interest to the Department and not covered by existing courses.
cilos: Equip with broad and useful knowledge to various topics which are not covered by existing courses.
(Each offering under the umbrella will have specific learning outcomes.)

CIVL 4210.title: Advanced Construction with AI and Robotics
CIVL 4210.description: This multi-faceted course encompasses advanced technologies in infrastructure and building construction, maintenance and operations. The course provides deep learning methods in computer vision and robot sensing with hands-on coding training on solving construction management problems with these methods. Combined with tools from AI and robotics, the course equips students with leading-edge knowledge and practices to bring about successful construction reform in the context of the smart city. The course is a mixture of lectures and student projects. The concept, theory and applications of AI and robotics in construction are delivered through lectures. The class also provides hands-on exercises on AI and robotics software development toolkits to learn how to apply these tools with given data. Through mini-projects, students explore the use of the toolkits for practical problem-solving in construction.
CIVL 4210.prerequisite: CIVL 1121 OR COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P (prior to 2025-26) OR COMP 1023
cilos: Apply AI tools to building and construction data.
Evaluate appropriateness of AI and robotics in building and infrastructure construction, maintenance, and operations.
Incorporate AI and robotics for practical construction engineering and management issues.

CIVL 4220.title: Scientific Machine Learning for Infrastructure Systems
CIVL 4220.description: Scientific machine learning (ML) seeks to address domain-specific data challenges and extract insights from scientific data sets through innovative methodological solutions, and this course aims to introduce scientific ML to senior students with a special focus on civil engineering applications. The course starts with an extensive review of statistics, the difference between ML and descriptive statistics, discusses sampling approaches for uncertainty quantification, then covers the fundamental knowledge of supervised learning (Bayesian linear regression, Gaussian processes, deep neural networks), unsupervised learning (k-means clustering, principal component analysis, Gaussian mixtures), and state space models (Kalman, particle filters). The course will further emphasize on the proper use of ML for civil engineering applications, including incorporating physics-based knowledge (physics-informed ML), dealing with data acquisition challenges (design of experiment, global optimization), and so on. Students will learn to address some unique challenges of applying ML to real-world engineering applications, preparing themselves better in their future career.
CIVL 4220.prerequisite: (CIVL 1121 OR COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P (prior to 2025-26) OR COMP 1023 OR COMP 1029P) AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350)
cilos: Represent uncertainty in parameters in civil engineering system models using probability and statistical techniques.
Solve basic supervised learning tasks, such as: regression, classification, and filtering; basic unsupervised learning tasks, such as: clustering, dimensionality reduction, and density estimation.
Create civil engineering domain-scientific machine learning models that encode existing physical information and other causal assumptions.
Apply basic Python software (e.g., numpy, scipy, scikit-learn) and advanced Python software (e.g., pytorch, Julia, Jax) for modelling and analyzing civil engineering systems.

CIVL 4240.title: Smart Infrastructure Sensing and Data Analytics
CIVL 4240.description: For students of the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department only. This course contains two modules. For sensing, it covers basic sensing technologies in structural engineering. Students will learn about traditional (e.g., accelerometers) as well as state-of-art sensing technologies (e.g., fiber optic sensing) and their practical applications in civil engineering. It also covers vibration-based structural health monitoring. Students will learn about the fundamentals of structural behavior, and analysis in the time and frequency domain. For data science, this course introduces fundamental knowledge and practical applications of data science and machine learning in the structural engineering context, primarily from understanding and extracting informative patterns from structural sensing data. Students will also learn about the use of relevant software & toolboxes (Python) to apply the discussed data science concepts on structural sensing datasets.
CIVL 4240.prerequisite: CIVL 1121 OR COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P (prior to 2025-26) OR COMP 2011 OR COMP 2012H OR COMP 1023
cilos: Describe the typical sensing technologies used in structural health monitoring.
Understand the fundamentals of fiber optic sensing technologies.
Understand structural behavior in frequency domain.
Understand the basic concepts of data science and machine learning.
Apply data science for practical structural engineering problems through the use of MATLAB and/or Python.

CIVL 4250.title: Project Management and Finance
CIVL 4250.description: This course introduces the basic methods, tools and techniques in managing and financing a project.  Management subjects cover project planning, cost management, time management, materials management, change management, construction labor, safety management, and communication management.  Financial subjects cover debt and equity finance, project risk analysis, cost and benefits of political risk insurance, project funding and cash flow, option pricing, and credit scoring of project finance debt.  Programming issues and Monte Carlo simulation for project management and finance models will also be discussed.
cilos: Aware of key issues in the project development cycle.
Gain fundamental knowledge in risk identification, allocation, and management.
Acquire basic skills in project funding and cash flow analysis.
Conduct financial and economic feasibility analysis in large-scale project development.

CIVL 4270.title: Construction Law and Contract Administration
CIVL 4270.description: This comprehensive course in Construction Law and Practice offers students a robust understanding of legal principles and their application in the construction industry as divided into four key areas: 1. Construction Law and Practice: Covers fundamentals, focusing on contracts and NEC4 and one case study. 2. Law in Context: Explores construction claims, including time and cost considerations under Hong Kong Government and NEC4 standard forms of contract and X29 Climate Change Option. 3. Public Private Partnerships (PPPs): Examines PPP structures in construction projects, including a Beijing Metro case study. 4. Dispute Resolution: Introduces all Alternative Dispute Resolution techniques, emphasizing the new Adjudication and Security of Payment legislation in Hong Kong. The course aims to equip students with practical knowledge and skills essential for navigating the complex landscape of construction law, preparing them for real-world challenges and further qualifications in the field.
cilos: Demonstrate awareness of construction law as both an academic discipline and a practical area in the construction industry.
Understand and explain the legal, historical, and theoretical frameworks relevant to construction law and contracts.
Analyze and manage construction claims and disputes within legal and contractual frameworks.

CIVL 4310.title: Energy System Modeling for Buildings and Cities
CIVL 4310.description: This course offers a comprehensive overview and practical exposure to energy system modelling for buildings and cities, emphasizing the significance of energy systems in contemporary infrastructure and their role in ensuring resilient, efficient, and sustainable civil engineering practices. The lectures will delve into fundamental physical concepts, mathematical principles, and software tools necessary for modelling energy systems in the context of cities and buildings. The theoretical aspects of the course will encompass foundational knowledge in heat transfer and building thermal dynamics. In parallel, the practical component of the course will introduce participants to an emerging equation-based programming language, utilizing Modelica as an illustrative example.
cilos: Analyze room-scale thermal dynamics and how to model it.
Analyze building-scale energy systems and how to model it.
Analyze district cooling and heating system and how to model it.
Apply the equation-based programming language Modelica and use it to solve real world problems.

CIVL 4320.title: Structural Steel Design
CIVL 4320.description: Limit state design of steel structures, stability analysis of thin-walled members, design of tension members, columns, beams, plate girders, beam-columns, structural connections, plastic analysis and design.
cilos: Understand the fundamental principles behind modern steel design code of practice.
Develop a basic understanding of various modes of failure of skeletal steel members and a comprehension of how these behaviors affect the performance of steel structures.
Demonstrate technical competency in designing steel members and connections using Hong Kong Steel Code of Practice.
Develop critical thinking skills in an open-ended design process with practical applications to real-world steel buildings.

CIVL 4330.title: Introduction to Structural Dynamics
CIVL 4330.description: Single degree of freedom systems, multi-degree of freedom systems, continuous systems, random vibrations, dynamic behavior under wind loads and earthquakes.
cilos: Understand basic concepts of Newton’s laws of motion.

Determine equations of motion (EOM) and structural response of single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) structural systems to various types of external excitation such as transient, harmonic and periodic driving forces.
Determine design parameters of SDOF systems such as damping ratio, dynamic magnification factor, and transmissibility during ground motion.
Assemble mass and stiffness matrices for multiple-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) systems; obtain frequencies of vibration and mode shapes and determine structural response of MDOF systems.
Solve vibration problems involving basic continuous systems such as beams and rods.
Understand Hamilton’s principle and Lagrange’s equations, and assemble stiffness matrices and EOM efficiently from related energy approach.
Analyze and design tuned-mass-dampers (TMD).
Understand and apply earthquake response spectra to analyze simple structures subjected to earthquakes.

CIVL 4340.title: Prestressed Concrete Design
CIVL 4340.description: Historical development; methods of prestressing, elastic analysis and design; flexural and shear capacity; losses of prestress; anchorage zones; composite members; design procedures and applications.
cilos: Understand and predict the behavior of prestressed concrete members.
Demonstrate the influence of time dependent effects on loss of prestressing of forces.
Design an appropriate prestressing system in a structural concrete member.
Propose general arrangement and provide detailing of proposed prestressing system.
Understand the importance and method of prestressing protection.

CIVL 4360.title: Implementing Artificial Intelligence in Smart Buildings
CIVL 4360.description: Modern smart infrastructure requires cutting-edge machine learning algorithms. This course offers a thorough exploration of fundamental machine learning concepts and provides hands-on experience in their application to smart infrastructure systems. Through the lectures, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the entire spectrum of machine learning, covering key aspects like data cleaning, pre-processing, and various machine learning techniques, and how those techniques can be applied to construct and maintain modern infrastructure. A prominent aspect of this course is its focus on real-world applications, particularly within the domain of smart infrastructure systems, e.g. occupants’ thermal preference prediction, crack detection, building load prediction, building energy system operation, etc. By exploring these applications, students will gain valuable insights into how machine learning can be effectively utilized in their future careers and research endeavors.
CIVL 4360.prerequisite: (CIVL 1121 OR COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P (prior to 2025-26) OR COMP 1023 OR COMP 1029P) AND (MATH 2111 OR MATH 2121 OR MATH 2131 OR MATH 2350)
cilos: Understand the domain knowledge of smart building, smart structures, and sustainable building operations.
Learn how variant machine learning algorithms can be applied in modern smart infrastructure systems.
Apply a variety of supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning algorithms to solve practical civil engineering problems.
Learn practical skills to improve machine learning models for the applications in civil engineering.

CIVL 4370.title: Computer Methods of Structural Analysis
CIVL 4370.description: Matrix formulation of structural analysis using stiffness method, solution of linear equations, applications to civil engineering structures, modeling of large and complex structural systems.
cilos: Idealize a civil engineering structure into a mechanical model (suitable for structural analysis).
Form the stiffness and loading matrices of an idealized structure, with a focus on building and bridge structures.
Perform a matrix structural analysis of an idealized structure with the help of a mathematical software.
Simulate and analyse a realistic civil engineering structure using a (commercially available) structural analysis software.

CIVL 4380.title: Introduction to Wind Effects on Buildings and Structures
CIVL 4380.description: Basic meteorology, structure of wind near the ground, wind induced vibrations, wind loading codes, wind tunnel test techniques.
cilos: Describe the characteristics of wind, wind structure near ground and topographical effects on wind.
Identify the factors that affect the structural design of a building against wind.
Determine the alongwind and crosswind forces of a structure and the wind-induced structural responses.
Analyse dynamic problem of buildings subject to different dynamic loads.
Perform a tall building design following Hong Kong and Australian wind codes.

CIVL 4430.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
CIVL 4430.description: This course describes relationship of environmental impact assessment (EIA) and environmental policy act; methods and procedures for environmental impact identification, prediction, evaluation and mitigation; contents in an EIA report.
cilos: Understand the purpose and role of EIA in the decision-making process where potential significant adverse environmental impacts can be addressed at an early stage.
Get familiar with the EIA planning, management, and procedures; environmental impact screening/scoping, identification, prediction, assessment, and avoidance/ minimization/compensation.
Know the contents of an EIA report according to the EIA Ordinance in Hong Kong.

CIVL 4450.title: Carbon Footprint Analysis and Reduction
CIVL 4450.description: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the sources and impacts of climate change, national and international policies, Kyoto Protocol, carbon credits and offset concepts. As engineers to be, students will also be able to calculate organization's carbon footprint, identify suitable mitigation strategies and provide carbon reduction solutions.
cilos: Know climate change basics and international and national climate and carbon targets and policies.
Understand carbon footprint concepts, carbon management concepts and procedures.
Explain carbon trading mechanisms and carbon offsetting projects.
Calculate corporate carbon footprint.
Identify and present carbon reduction solutions.
Form its own judgment on the climate change issues and find solutions in both international and local contexts.

CIVL 4460.title: Process Design of Environmental Engineering Facilities
CIVL 4460.description: Basic principles in the process design of environmental engineering facilities, such as water and wastewater treatment systems, pump station, as well as sanitary landfill disposal.
cilos: Understand the principles involved in the design of water and wastewater treatment facilities and their major components, including concepts, design criteria, design practice of major unit operation and unit process as well as an entire water or wastewater plant.
Make use of mathematical or quantitative methods to design the major components and the whole processes of water and wastewater treatment.

Apply the principles learned in this course for the design and management of the components of the water and wastewater treatment systems, including concepts, design criteria, design practice of major unit operation and unit process as well as an entire water or wastewater plant.

CIVL 4470.title: Air Quality Control and Management
CIVL 4470.description: Historical and health impact studies related to air pollution. Atmospheric stability and its impact on the transport and dispersion of pollutants. Sources of major air pollutants. Comparison of urban, industrial and transport related air pollution issues, using Hong Kong and Pearl River Delta as examples. Control of stationary and mobile emission sources. Air quality management - framework, policy tools and comparison of different approaches.
cilos: Identify the roots of air pollution and its impact.
Describe how atmospheric meteorology affects the transport, transformation and dispersion of the air pollutants.
Formulate general ideas in air pollution control.
Assess critically current air quality management methods.
Apply air quality models to describe different air pollution problems.
Adopt new advance and opportunities in air quality control and management.
Transit better to a professional career and/or graduate school related to air quality control and management.

CIVL 4480.title: Climate Modeling and Risk Assessment
CIVL 4480.description: Climate models are the complex mathematical representation of the major climate system components (e.g. atmosphere, ocean, land surface, etc) and their interactions. Climate models have proved to be the most valuable tools in understanding climate processes that determine the response of the climate system to anthropogenic forcings, such as increases in greenhouse gases concentrations and land use changes. This course provides an introduction to the physical principles of climate model as well as all procedures related to climate modeling. Some classes will be taught in the computer laboratory, where students will perform their own simulations using web-based climate model and analyze the results. In addition, this course explores the challenge of understanding and managing the risks of climate extremes.
CIVL 4480.prerequisite: MATH 1003 OR MATH 1012 (prior to 2025-26) OR MATH 1013 OR MATH 1020 OR MATH 1023
cilos: Demonstrate a solid understanding of the Earth's climate system.
Describe greenhouse effect and its association with global warming.
Describe the structure of climate model and general procedure of climate modeling.
Describe how to analyze the performance and uncertainty of climate simulations.
Understand the reliability of climate model and interpret the simulation results based on the basic principles governing climate system.
Describe the key concepts and definitions relating to disaster risk management and adaptation to climate change.
Identify and assess the risk as a function of vulnerability and exposure.
Understand the approaches for reducing and managing disaster risk in a changing climate.

CIVL 4520.title: Municipal Hydrosystems Engineering and Management
CIVL 4520.description: The course integrates the knowledge of hydrology, hydraulics, statistics, economics, and optimization in the dealing with municipal hydrosystems engineering and management. In particular, focuses will be given to quantity aspect of water supplies and water excesses. The hydrosystems to be covered include water distribution, urban sewage and stormwater drainage, reservoirs/detention facilities, pumps, etc.
cilos: Acquire the basic knowledge of municipal hydrosystems engineering and management.
Understand the engineering aspects of water supply and distribution, with background of hydrology, pipe flow hydraulics, and economical considerations.
Understand the engineering design of stormwater drainage systems, with background of runoff estimation and gradually varied open channel flow.
Acquire the knowledge of stormwater management devices including storm sewers, culverts, spillways, reservoirs and pumps.
Appreciate the assimilative capacity of the natural environment, through the study of basic concepts of turbulent mixing and dispersion of pollutants in rivers.

CIVL 4560.title: Urban Hydroclimate and the Built Environment
CIVL 4560.description:
This course is a mixture of lecture, reading, and group project focused on urban hydroclimate and the built environment, particularly their interactions through the energy-water-climate nexus. Lectures will cover mathematical laws and physical concepts of heat, moisture and mass transport in the built environment, as well as implications of urban hydroclimate on smart city development in the 21st century. Through hands-on tutorials, students will learn a numerical model and use it to explore the impact of neighborhood design on urban thermal environment, including
the usage of novel engineering materials, urban landscape and building technology.
cilos: Formulate and solve heat, moisture, and mass transport problems in the built environment using governing equations.
Describe the water-energy-climate nexus in cities.
Conduct neighborhood planning and sustainability analysis through numerical models.
Identify the hydroclimate challenges cities face in the near future and their potential engineering solutions.
Understand the broad impact of engineering infrastructure on urban development and environmental sustainability.

CIVL 4610.title: Introduction to Data Analytics for Smart Transportation Systems
CIVL 4610.description: This course covers the role of stochasticity in transport systems and the methods used to account for this within transport infrastructure assessment, with a particular focus on the application of data analysis methods. The course introduces how to analyze the performance of public transport systems and road network using classic queuing theory and travel time reliability concepts. The course will complement skills learnt in the other transport courses to provide a well-rounded knowledge of smart transport planning and management. The focus is on the application of transport models in real world settings using real data. Students have the opportunity to work with large open source data in two experiential-learning projects. The course also develops skills for working with data and managing collaborative projects.
CIVL 4610.prerequisite: CIVL 1121 OR COMP 1021 OR COMP 1022P (prior to 2025-26) OR COMP 1023 OR COMP 2011 OR COMP 2012H
cilos: Learn the fundamental knowledge of queuing theory and reliability and stochastic characteristics of transport systems.
Learn how to work with large open-source data in Python and how to use visualization tools and data mining techniques.
Learn how to design a research question, methodology and data approach for a real problem.
Learn in-depth knowledge in queuing theory and performance evaluation of urban transportation systems.
Work in teams in the second part of the course and present their work in a poster showcase/presentation session.

Work on real data obtained from either government website or APIs, and utilize transport models to evaluate existing public transport and road network performance, identify current issues, and propose transport policy implications.
